name: EST delayed sell-burn drained by skim loop
summary: ESTToken books every taxed transfer into the pair as a pending sell burn; the next non-pair transfer burns that amount, capped at 10% of the pair's EST, from the pair and syncs, even if the tokens were skimmed back out. The attacker looped transfer-to-pair and skim about 150 times, shrinking the pair's EST to dust, and sold EST for its WBNB.
notes: Immutable token; the pair, BNBDeposit's fee exclusion and minSupply were set at construction and later owner calls do not touch the burn path, so deployment sets the age.
Loss is the pair's net WBNB depletion in the transaction, with the attacker's WBNB entering through BNBDeposit netted as inflow; the pair's EST side is not valued separately.
No other transaction burned the pair's EST more than twice (pair-to-zero Transfer logs per transaction), so the anchor is the first and only exploit.
